In this section, you will learn about selective breeding, particularly genomic selection along with 
the statistical models implemented across the `masreml` and `masbayes` packages.

## Pages

1.  [From Phenotype to Genome](from-phenotype-to-genome.qmd): Background
    on the move from phenotype + pedigree BLUP to genomic selection. Five sub-pages cover
    traditional / MAS, the GS revolution, the methodology bridge,
    implementation across livestock, and future directions.
2.  [Biallelic & Multi-allelic](biallelic-and-multiallelic.qmd): How the
    genotype matrix is built differently for SNP (biallelic) vs
    microhaplotype (multi-allelic) data, and what each construction
    feeds downstream.
3.  [Mixed Model & BLUP Family
    (Frequency-based)](mixed-model-blup-family.qmd): Models such as
    PBLUP, GBLUP, GWABLUP will be explained with one mixed model
    equation (MME) and three relationship matrices.
4.  [Bayesian Alphabet (Probabilistic)](bayesian-alphabet.qmd): Includes
    the BayesA (scaled inverse-$\chi^2$) and BayesR (4-component
    mixture) models.
5.  [Continuous and Binary Trait](continuous-and-binary-trait.qmd): What
    changes when the response is binary? So, liability-scale modelling,
    Laplace approximation in `masreml`, Albert-Chib augmentation in
    `masbayes`, and the observed-versus-liability heritability transform
    will be described.

::: callout-note
Every "See it in code" section uses the [bundled demo
dataset](../input-data/index.qmd) and calls only real exported functions
of `masreml` / `masbayes` (cross-checked against the package source).
:::
